# Gate 1 package - BI-PF-1271
**Eventing SSOT (Go): alert policy - rules, throttle, escalation**

## Plain language
**What/why:** Alert routing is inline in orchestration_context._POLICY; no persisted rules, throttling, or escalation. -> A policy engine mapping event type/severity -> channels with throttle and escalation (reusing the policy map).

## Gate 0 reconciliation + impact
RECONCILIATION - BI-PF-1271
  prior_decisions : ['docs/EVENTING-ALERTING-SSOT-DESIGN.md: Alerting SSOT architecture sec 4, 5, 9 Phase 6; Go core with PostgreSQL SoR.', 'BI-PF-1265 Epic: System-wide eventing SSOT and decoupled subscription infrastructure.']
  existing_path   : ['core/orchestration_context.py:11-21 (_POLICY dictionary with hardcoded alert types and channels)', 'go/eventtransport/notify.go:72-87 (priorityOf string matching)']
  assumptions     : ['Slide-window throttle tracking by tenant_id + rule_id + fingerprint is stored in memory and persisted in alert_throttle_state table.', 'Default channel routing aligns with Notify, Email, Webhook, HIL, and Backlog channel types.']
  divergences     : ['None. Extends inline hardcoded policy dictionary into fully persisted rule-based Go engine as specified in master design.']
  open_questions  : []
IMPACT REVIEW
  claim | verdict | evidence | recommendation
  alert policy engine in Go with persisted rules, sliding throttle, and escalation | aligned | docs/EVENTING-ALERTING-SSOT-DESIGN.md: sec 4, 5, 9 Phase 6; go/edpdata/alert_policy.go | Implement in Go under productforge/edpdata with PostgreSQL SoR and in-memory mock
  language decision: Go for new alert policy logic and stores; Python for API router registration | aligned | scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py: Go for new data/service logic, existing Python for API routes | Implement Go policy engine and alert stores in go/edpdata/; mount endpoints in api/routers/events.py
  API CHECK: alert rules CRUD and policy evaluation endpoints | aligned | api/routers/events.py; api/openapi.json | Expose GET/POST/DELETE /events/alert-rules and POST /events/alert-policy/evaluate with require_operator auth
  AC acceptance criteria verification | aligned | go/edpdata/alert_policy_test.go; tests/test_alert_policy_api.py | Verify 5 detailed ACs through Go unit tests and Python API integration tests

## Current stage
**planning**

## Gate 1.5 findings + architect recommendation
Gate 1.5 - Findings & Dispositions (model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=fc0ca113fb56)
**Overall architect recommendation: APPROVE**
Findings: 3 (BLOCKER 0 / MAJOR 0 / MINOR 2 / NIT 1); dispositions: actioned 3; all blockers/majors actioned
status: PENDING | ACTIONED | ACCEPTED | DEFERRED | REJECTED | SCOPE

| # | Severity | Finding | Disposition | Response / resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MINOR | Ensure sliding throttle state cleanup or TTL expiration mechanism so long-running processes do not accumulate unbounded fingerprint entries in memory. | ACTIONED | Implement CleanupExpired(now, ttl) in memory cache with periodic sweep and window_expires_at index in SQL. |
| 2 | MINOR | Provide clear logging when fallback default policy is engaged due to database rule retrieval failure. | ACTIONED | Emit structured warning log alert_policy_db_fallback_engaged with tenant and error details. |
| 3 | NIT | Add helper method for batch evaluation of multiple events against alert policy. | ACTIONED | Implement EvaluateBatch(events []Event) []AlertDecision on Go AlertPolicyEngine. |

--- SUMMARY (review) ---
  Design for BI-PF-1271 is robust, modular, and fully aligned with EOS and Eventing SSOT architecture.
  Multi-tenancy, sliding throttle windows, and escalation channels are well-defined.
  Language rule (Go for edpdata engine, Python for API routing) strictly respected. No blockers.
